## Proof

**Setup.** Place the regular hexagon $G\text{-}O\text{-}B\text{-}E\text{-}A\text{-}R$ (side length $2$, so circumradius $2$) centered at the origin, with vertices in clockwise order:
$$G=(0,2),\ O=(\sqrt3,1),\ B=(\sqrt3,-1),\ E=(0,-2),\ A=(-\sqrt3,-1),\ R=(-\sqrt3,1).$$
One checks $|GO|=\sqrt{3+1}=2$, and $G,B,A$ form an equilateral triangle of side $2\sqrt3$.

**Trajectories.** Each drone crawls clockwise $1$ km (half a side). Let $t\in[0,1]$ parametrize the journey, with position $=$ start $+\,t\,(\text{midpoint}-\text{start})$:
$$V_1(t)=\Big(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}t,\ 2-\tfrac{t}{2}\Big),\quad V_2(t)=\Big(\sqrt3\big(1-\tfrac{t}{2}\big),\ -1-\tfrac{t}{2}\Big),\quad V_3(t)=\big(-\sqrt3,\ -1+t\big).$$
Each $V_i(t)=V_i(0)+t\,d_i$ is **linear** in $t$.

**Key reduction.** A point inside $T(t)$ has barycentric form $\alpha V_1(t)+\beta V_2(t)+\gamma V_3(t)$ with $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=1$, $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\ge0$. Substituting the linear motion:
$$\alpha V_1(0)+\beta V_2(0)+\gamma V_3(0)+t\big(\alpha d_1+\beta d_2+\gamma d_3\big).$$
This is a **linear** map from the convex polytope $\{(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,t):\alpha+\beta+\gamma=1,\ \alpha,\beta,\gamma\ge0,\ 0\le t\le1\}$ (a triangular prism) into $\mathbb{R}^2$. The image of a convex polytope under a linear map is the convex hull of the images of its vertices. The prism has $6$ vertices, mapping to $V_1(0),V_1(1),V_2(0),V_2(1),V_3(0),V_3(1)$. Therefore
$$\text{swept region}=\operatorname{conv}\{V_1(0),V_1(1),V_2(0),V_2(1),V_3(0),V_3(1)\}.$$

**The six points.** Computing endpoints:
$$P_1=(0,2),\ P_2=\Big(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2},\tfrac32\Big),\ P_3=(\sqrt3,-1),\ P_4=\Big(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2},-\tfrac32\Big),\ P_5=(-\sqrt3,-1),\ P_6=(-\sqrt3,0).$$

**All six are extreme.** Checking each "intermediate" point against the chord skipping it: $P_2$ lies to the left of $\overrightarrow{P_1P_3}$ (cross product $=\sqrt3>0$), $P_4$ lies to the left of $\overrightarrow{P_3P_5}$ (cross product $=\sqrt3>0$), $P_6$ lies to the left of $\overrightarrow{P_5P_1}$ (cross product $=\sqrt3>0$). Hence all six points are vertices of the convex hull, in clockwise order $P_1\to P_2\to P_3\to P_4\to P_5\to P_6$.

**Area via shoelace.**
$$2A=\left|\sum x_i y_{i+1}-x_{i+1}y_i\right|$$
Computing each consecutive pair:
- $P_1P_2$: $0\cdot\tfrac32-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot2=-\sqrt3$
- $P_2P_3$: $\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot(-1)-\sqrt3\cdot\tfrac32=-2\sqrt3$
- $P_3P_4$: $\sqrt3\cdot(-\tfrac32)-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot(-1)=-\sqrt3$
- $P_4P_5$: $\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot(-1)-(-\sqrt3)\cdot(-\tfrac32)=-2\sqrt3$
- $P_5P_6$: $(-\sqrt3)\cdot0-(-\sqrt3)\cdot(-1)=-\sqrt3$
- $P_6P_1$: $(-\sqrt3)\cdot2-0\cdot0=-2\sqrt3$

Sum $=-(1+2+1+2+1+2)\sqrt3=-9\sqrt3$, so
$$A=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 9\sqrt3=\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}.$$

**Sanity check.** Initial triangle area $=3\sqrt3\approx5.20$; final triangle area $=\frac{9\sqrt3}{4}\approx3.90$; swept area $\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}\approx7.79$ exceeds both, as expected.

$$\boxed{\dfrac{9\sqrt3}{2}}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE

$$\alpha V_1(0)+\beta V_2(0)+\gamma V_3(0)+t\big(\alpha d_1+\beta d_2+\gamma d_3\big).$$
This is a **linear** map from the convex polytope $\{(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,t):\alpha+\beta+\gamma=1,\ \alpha,\beta,\gamma\ge0,\ 0\le t\le1\}$ (a triangular prism) into $\mathbb{R}^2$.
